why: The project's 50 MW IT load assumes an N+1 configuration of 21 diesel generators at 2,500 kW each, yielding a computed NOx potential to emit of 185 tpy under the assumptions of 500 hours per year operation and 6.4 g/kWh NOx (Tier 2 diesel). This NOx potential exceeds the 100 tpy major-source threshold defined in 40 CFR 70.2, triggering a federal Title V operating permit requirement. The project's 50 MW load falls below the 75 MW threshold for both Texas SB 6 large-load interconnection standards and the Governor's ERCOT data center audit, so those state-level requirements do not apply. No local political barriers such as county moratoria are identified in the findings for this incorporated Abilene site.

needs_confirmation.text: The why-chain treats the computed NOx PTE of 185 tpy as fact, but this value depends on undisclosed project-specific design choices: generator count (21), unit size (2,500 kW), fuel type (diesel), emission tier (Tier 2), and annual operating hours (500 h/yr). The project may use natural gas generators, Tier 4 diesel, fewer units, or accept a 100-hour/year operational limit, any of which could reduce NOx PTE below the 100 tpy major-source threshold and flip the finding from 'applies: yes' to 'applies: no'.

needs_confirmation.text: The finding states the audit requirement applies only above a 75 MW threshold, but the cited evidence quote states 'The PUCT and ERCOT must complete this audit before any data center project moves forward,' with no mention of a 75 MW threshold. If the Governor's directive applies to all data center projects regardless of size, the finding's 'applies: no' conclusion is incorrect and the audit would be a prerequisite for this 50 MW project as well.
needs_confirmation.question: Does the Governor's audit directive explicitly limit its scope to loads >75 MW, or does 'any data center project' mean all sizes?
